Triage: promoted to `pm:queue`, type Bug — one declaration must yield one behaviour on both render paths (the #3272/#3400/#3402/#3404/#3439 family), and `max_length` is a live authoring spelling on the exact path (hand-written `FormSchema`) that has no normalizing producer in between. Scope ruling to keep this dispatchable without a design decision: **the ceiling-parsing half only** — dual-read `maxLength ?? max_length` in the built-in `input` branch the way PR #5200 did for `textarea`, and keep `max_length` out of the DOM (add it to `stripRendererOnlyProps` if that is the mechanism). The visible counter / accessible-limit half for single-line inputs is **not** commissioned — if the implementer believes it is inseparable, stop and report rather than widening.

Dedup note: the filer could not search at filing time (API rate limit). This seat's spot-check against the known family cards found no open duplicate for the `input`-branch ceiling; if one surfaces, merge there.

Note this file is a hot spot with two landings today (#3439/PR5200, #4259/PR5238), so **re-verify at your claim** and take every anchor from the tree.

## Zone 1 — triage's scope ruling, and it is a cliff not a preference

> Scope ruling to keep this dispatchable without a design decision: **the ceiling-parsing half only** — dual-read `maxLength ?? max_length` in the built-in `input` branch the way PR #5200 did for `textarea`, and keep `max_length` out of the DOM (add it to `stripRendererOnlyProps` if that is the mechanism). The visible counter / accessible-limit half for single-line inputs is **not** commissioned — if the implementer believes it is inseparable, stop and report rather than widening.

⛔ **No counter, no accessible-limit announcement, no `aria-describedby` wiring for a limit** on the single-line input. The card is explicit that whether a single-line input should carry a visible count is an independent design trade-off that does **not** follow from the textarea conclusion. The ceiling-parsing half is mechanical; the counter half is not. If you conclude they cannot be separated, **stop and report** — do not widen.

## Premise — verified on `origin/main` this round

The defect holds, and the reference implementation is in the same file:

```
form.tsx:3078   const { max_length: _maxLengthLegacy, ...textareaProps } = fieldProps as any;
form.tsx:3079   const maxLength = (fieldProps as any).maxLength ?? (fieldProps as any).max_length;
form.tsx:3080   const rest = stripRendererOnlyProps(textareaProps);
```

That is the `case 'textarea'` branch after PR5200. The built-in `case 'input'` branch does none of it — it spreads `stripRendererOnlyProps(fieldProps)` and never reads the declared ceiling, so `max_length: 50` produces **no cap at all** plus a stray, inert `max_length="50"` attribute (invalid HTML), while `maxLength: 50` works only by the coincidence that it happens to be a valid DOM attribute name.

Line numbers **will** have moved — this file took two landings today. Take them from the tree.

## One judgement the ruling leaves you, and I want it decided deliberately

Triage wrote *"add it to `stripRendererOnlyProps` if that is the mechanism"*. **The in-file precedent does not do that** — PR5200 used a **local destructure** (`const { max_length: _maxLengthLegacy, ...textareaProps }`) rather than extending the shared strip list.

That difference matters: `stripRendererOnlyProps` is shared by **every** branch, so adding `max_length` there changes what reaches the DOM for widgets you are not fixing and have not tested. The local destructure is the narrower, reversible choice and it is what the neighbouring code already does.

**Follow the local-destructure precedent** unless you find a concrete reason not to — and if you do use the shared list, enumerate every branch it affects and say why that is safe. ⛔ Do not make a repo-wide behaviour change as a side effect of a one-branch fix.

## Why this is a real user-facing defect and not style

`max_length` is a **live authoring spelling**, not a fossil: `TextAreaField` on the registered path dual-reads it (framework#1878 §3), three form-field producers dual-read and normalise to `maxLength` (`ObjectForm.tsx`, `sectionFields.ts`, `EmbeddableForm.applyDefaultMaxLengths`), and `packages/types/src/field-types.ts` declares it on several field types. Every reader in the repo honours it **except this branch** — and this branch is exactly the one serving hand-written `FormSchema` fed straight to the renderer, where there is **no normalising producer in between**. On that path the author *is* the producer.

## Tests

- `max_length: 50` on a built-in `input` yields `maxlength="50"` on the element, and **no** stray `max_length` attribute. Assert both halves — the missing cap and the invalid attribute are two distinct defects and a test that only checks the cap would let the stray attribute survive.
- `maxLength: 50` keeps working (it does today, by coincidence — pin it so the fix cannot break the spelling that accidentally worked).
- Both spellings together: `maxLength` wins, matching `maxLength ?? max_length`.
- Neither declared: no `maxlength` attribute at all, no stray attribute.
- Assert via `getAttributeNames()` / `getAttribute('maxlength')`, the way the card measured it — that is what makes the stray-attribute half observable.

Reverse-verify: restore the branch, keep the tests, predict the reds **before** running, report predicted vs observed.

## Dedup — the filer could not do it

The card records that `search_issues` / `list_issues` returned `API rate limit already exceeded` three times at filing, so the required pre-file dedup **never ran**. My spot-check against the family cards found no open duplicate for the `input`-branch ceiling. **Do one more check before you start** — if an open duplicate surfaces, merge there and report rather than landing a second fix.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only** — here derive from `.github/workflows` and `package.json`. Changeset required (`@object-ui/components`); `patch` or `minor`, ⛔ never `major`.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn.** Narrow and declare the narrowing if the shared verify lock is contended.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5201`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.
